title: Patch 2.68.1 QA
eyebrow: QA for house-rules 2.68.1, the first step of the plugin restructure · ready for your test

short.lead: All five steps of the 2.68.1 patch are built and committed on the branch ccr-7dcf4ee2-zp3mm8. Each step first added a test to verify.py (the repo's self-check script) that reproduces its incident from the issue "the design loop is broken and blocks sessions" (#303), then fixed it. The full verify.py suite passed twice in a row with 839 checks, up from 832, and tools/verify_tools.py passed its 47 checks. I also ran two real nested Claude Code sessions here with the patched plugin loaded and the installed 2.68.0 copy switched off. In the first, one message holding both approvals moved the stage to Plan, with the feature named "test feature". In the second, a 307-word reply got the page report instead of a page block. The editor and evidence checks, which this patch doesn't change, still asked for their fixes. Your test confirms the same on your own machine after the update.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what was built and how it was checked.
items: Every approval in a message is read

The issue "the design loop reads every approval in a message, and a design approval sets the feature name" (#307), commit 2e9c71b. Your message "Design approved: importer.  Build plan approved: Importer" now moves the stage to Plan, and the build plan is refused with its own reason. After "QA failed: Importer", "Design approved: Importer" counts as the redo even when the saved feature name is out of date. Both cases failed on the old code first.

The issue "the design loop records only issues created in its own repo" (#308), commit dea8e47. An issue made in another repo gets a note and isn't recorded; one made in the checkout's own GitHub repo is recorded as before. Both cases failed on the old code first, checked by reversing the patch and running the suite.
Four checks report instead of blocking

The issue "four checks report instead of blocking, and the page builder accepts any approval line" (#309), commit 9868f29. Writes made through the command line while code is locked now go through with a report. The re-creation note asks for nothing. The page checkpoint reports instead of blocking. Bare references (an issue number or option letter with nothing naming what it points at) go to you in a one-line report. make_page.py builds any approval line, with a note that the line moves no stage. Eleven existing cases that expected a block were updated to expect the report.
A page reminder survives a shorter retry

The issue "a blocked page stays owed across retries" (#310), commit 9868f29. The way a flagged reply slipped past the reminder today is replayed: a 70-word retry after a flagged 165-word reply still gets the report, a linked page clears it, and a new message from you starts with nothing owed.
Five steps on your desktop, about ten minutes

The issue "release the patch with its version, docs and QA page" (#311), commit fa7ff2a. Every command below runs in Windows PowerShell, opened from the Start menu; none needs a particular folder. Step 1: on GitHub, open the pull request "house-rules 2.68.1: unblock the design loop before the restructure" (#312) and press Merge pull request. Step 2: run claude plugin marketplace update aj-house-rules, then claude plugin update house-rules@aj-house-rules, then claude plugin list. Pass: the list shows house-rules at version 2.68.1. Step 3: make a throwaway test repo with New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force "$HOME\hr-test\docs\6-decisions" | Out-Null; git init -q "$HOME\hr-test"; Set-Content "$HOME\hr-test\docs\6-decisions\Decisions.md" "# Decisions", then start Claude there with Set-Location "$HOME\hr-test"; claude. Step 4: in that session, type exactly: Design approved: test feature.  Build plan approved: test feature. Then exit Claude and run Get-Content "$HOME\hr-test\.claude\house-rules-loop.json". Pass: the text contains "stage": "plan" and "feature": "test feature". Fail: "stage": "design", or no file. Step 5: start claude in the same folder again and type: Explain in about 250 words how git branches work. Pass: no message says "reply is not done yet" with a line starting "- page:". Messages naming the editor or evidence checks are expected and don't count.
Reply "QA passed: plugin restructure 2.68.1 patch", or "QA failed" with the step number that failed and what you saw.

changes: Every approval phrase is applied in stage order.
One phrase read, and a refusal ended the message.
Design, then build plan, then QA, each with its own note.
A new function, _loop_apply, splits the message into approval phrases. The old code now lives in _loop_apply_one, which handles one phrase.
Each issue's repo is compared with the checkout's GitHub origin (the GitHub address this local copy came from).
Only the checkout's own repo counts; others get a note.
A checkout with no GitHub origin counts every issue, as before, because nothing names its repo.
Four checks and the approval line.
They blocked or demanded a resend.
They report what they would have blocked.
In the checkpoint table, the page row is now marked as report-only. The writing check keeps its other kinds of finding.

unverified: No real session has run the 2.68.1 hooks: this session runs the installed 2.68.0 plugin, so every check above comes from verify.py's replays of hook calls, not a live session

The cross-repo issue check was replayed against a test fixture (a made-up repo) whose origin is github.com/me/own. A real session with two repos attached was not tried. That is the case in the issue "Design-loop approvals are dropped silently when the session folder isn't a git repo" (#296)
A checkout with no GitHub origin still counts every issue, so a session working outside a GitHub clone could still mix repos
The file counts below are taken from git after the build; no separate estimate was made beforehand

claude-house-rules/plugins/house-rules/s: the approval parser (#307), the issue record (#308), three report-only checks (#309) and the page memory (#310)
the new cases for every step, and the updated cases that expected a block
docs/4-systems/design-loop.md: approvals, the issue record, the code lock and long replies

wrapup.summary: The 2.68.1 patch is built: approvals in one message are all read, other repos' issues don't count, four checks report instead of blocking, and a flagged page stays owed.
wrapup.changing: Files changed: scripts/hook.py, scripts/make_page.py, verify.py, the plugin version, and the design-loop, clear-writing and state docs.
wrapup.blocking: Your test in a new session after the merge and update.
wrapup.next: After QA passes, we hold the grilling session, where I question you on the design before building, on the 28 rule contradictions. Then come the restructure's own steps, tracked as sub-issues (smaller issues linked under a parent) of the issue "restructure into a shared core with project boundaries and six optional sub-plugins" (#306).
